methods.description: Read given marks or stated side, angle and diagonal properties; match, state, compare or identify the special quadrilateral without treating missing marks as negative evidence.
Use equal diagonals and diagonal bisection to find a full or half diagonal length, giving the property as a reason.
Use the diagonal of a rhombus bisecting a vertex angle to find the whole angle from one half.
Decide whether a property is always true; distinguish guaranteed properties from possible special cases and give a counterexample when a general claim fails.

review.theoryObservation: The diagonal definition, inclusive kite/trapezium facts and guarantees versus possible special cases are correct and agree with the accepted classification prerequisite. I independently checked all34 solution texts: no repeated procedure-label headers are present, and the first two repaired steps now read stated givens before applying properties instead of inferring a name or negative property from absent marks. The unchanged third step remains coherent. All four methods map to every final item and have genuine examples: read/match marks and comparisons E0/E1, diagonal length E2, vertex-angle bisection E3, always-true/counterexample E4. E0 most-specific-guaranteed wording properly allows a square special case; E1 need-not wording avoids exclusive-family errors. E2/E3 are valid source-adapted numerical contrasts, not practice copies; no incidental equal roles or advanced method introduced. All existing legitimate narrow sets, givens and units remain.
review.sourceObservation: Read all five complete final refs: Stage4 syllabus2509–2533; original diagonal definition100–114; complete marked-figure/table investigation168–228; Foundation5a–f275–301; full Development9a–o358–409. Actually viewed all8 original PNGs6,11–16,33. PNGs11/12/13 confirm square equal/perpendicular/bisected, rectangle equal/bisected, rhombus perpendicular/bisected properties. PNGs14/15/16 confirm parallelogram bisection, kite one-way perpendicular bisection and the trapezium example. The table explicitly asks always true: No is not never. Its transcribed rectangle adjacent-side-equality and rhombus adjacent-perpendicularity cells conflict with definitions and actual marked figures; the author correctly excludes those errors while preserving raw evidence. PNG33 is the complete15-part source composite. Its rectangle partl5cm label has ambiguous whole/half association versus the3/4side outline; the new explicit whole AC21.4cm example avoids importing that ambiguity. The source half-angle30degree rhombus supports the37→74 adapted example. No claim about unseen original DOCX/PDF errors; source methods and familiar language remain within introductory Stage4, with no Pythagoras or formal proof expansion. No unavailable-image exceptions or removals.
